Apple___Apple_scab.description: Apple scab is a fungal disease that causes dark, scabby lesions on apple leaves and fruit.
symptoms: Dark, scabby lesions on leaves and fruit
treatment: Apply fungicides containing captan or mancozeb
Use organic fungicides like copper spray or neem oil
prevention: Keep the area around apple trees clean and free of fallen leaves and fruit

Apple___Black_rot.description: Black rot is a serious fungal disease in apple trees that causes dark, sunken lesions on fruit, leaves and bark.
symptoms: Dark, sunken lesions on fruit, leaves and bark
treatment: Application of fungicides like mancozeb or captan
Removal and destruction of infected plant parts
prevention: Regular pruning to improve air circulation

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: Cedar apple rust is a fungal disease that affects apples, causing yellow spots and galls on leaves, fruit, and twigs.
symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on leaves and fruit
Galls or horn-like structures on twigs and branches
treatment: Apply fungicides that contain myclobutanil or propiconazole
Pruning and burning infected branches
prevention: Regular inspections and removal of nearby cedar trees

Apple___healthy.description: The plant looks healthy and vigorous.
treatment: Maintain regular watering
Monitor for pests

Cassava CB (Cassava Blight).description: Cassava CB is a fungal disease that causes wilting and yellowing of leaves in cassava plants.
treatment: Apply fungicides containing copper sulfate
Use organic fungicides like neem oil
prevention: Practice crop rotation to reduce disease buildup in soil

Cassava CM (Cassava Mosaic).description: Cassava Mosaic is a viral disease causing reduced yield and quality in Cassava plants.
treatment: Use of antiviral chemicals like Oxymatrine
Removal and destruction of infected plants
prevention: Regular field inspection and removal of infected plants

bacterial_leaf_blight.description: Bacterial leaf blight is a plant disease caused by bacteria that results in yellowing and wilting of leaves.
symptoms: Brown spots or blight on leaves
treatment: Use of copper-based fungicides
Application of organic bactericides like Serenade
prevention: Regular inspection and removal of infected plants
Crop rotation to reduce bacteria in soil

bacterial_leaf_streak.description: Bacterial leaf streak is a disease caused by bacteria that results in brown or yellow streaks on plant leaves.
symptoms: Water-soaked spots on leaves that dry and turn brown
treatment: Use copper-based bactericides
Application of organic bactericides like Serenade
prevention: Regularly inspect plants for early signs of disease
Avoid overhead watering to prevent moisture build-up which encourages bacterial growth

bacterial_panicle_blight.description: Bacterial panicle blight is a rice disease caused by the bacterium Burkholderia glumae that affects the panicle, leading to grain sterility and crop loss.
symptoms: Brown discoloration of glumes and grains
treatment: Use of copper-based fungicides
Application of antibiotics like Streptomycin
prevention: Maintain field sanitation by removing infected plants
Monitor fields regularly for early detection

blast.description: Blast is a plant disease caused by the fungus Magnaporthe oryzae, primarily affecting crops like rice, wheat, and barley.
symptoms: Light gray to white lesions on leaves
treatment: Use fungicides such as Tricyclazole and Isoprothiolane
Apply organic biocontrol agents like Trichoderma
prevention: Maintain proper field sanitation and avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization

brown_spot.description: Brown spot is a fungal disease causing brown or tan lesions on leaves and stems.
symptoms: Brown or tan spots on leaves
treatment: Use of fungicides such as Trifloxystrobin
Applying organic fungicides like copper sprays
prevention: Avoiding overwatering and ensuring good soil drainage

dead_heart.description: Dead heart is a plant disease usually affecting rice, causing the central leaf whorl to wither and die.
symptoms: Dieback beginning from the plant's heart
treatment: Use of appropriate insecticides like fipronil and imidacloprid
Introducing natural predators of the disease-causing pests
prevention: Regular field monitoring and early pest detection
Rotational planting to disrupt pest lifecycle

downy_mildew.description: Downy mildew is a fungal disease that causes yellowing leaves, stunted growth, and a fluffy white or gray mold on the undersides of leaves.
symptoms: Yellow or light green spots on top of leaves
White or gray mold on the underside of leaves
treatment: Apply fungicides like metalaxyl and mefenoxam
Organic treatments include sprays containing copper or sulfur
prevention: Ensure good air circulation around plants to reduce humidity

hispa.description: Hispa is a pest that attacks rice plants, causing severe damage to the leaves and overall crop yield.
symptoms: White or yellow spots on the leaves
treatment: Apply an appropriate insecticide such as Chlorpyrifos or Cartap hydrochloride
Use of bio-pesticides like Beauveria bassiana or Metarhizium anisopliae
prevention: Regularly monitor the field for early signs of hispa

tungro.description: Tungro is a viral disease often seen in rice crops, causing yellowing and stunted growth.

Application of organic fungicides
prevention: Regular monitoring and early detection of infected plants
Use of clean and certified seeds

Leaves turn yellow and dry out
Severe infection can lead to premature leaf drop
treatment: Use fungicides containing sulfur, potassium bicarbonate or neem oil

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Gray leaf spot is a fungal disease in corn that causes grayish tan lesions on the leaves.
treatment: Use of fungicides like triazoles and strobilurins
Crop rotation with non-host plants
prevention: Regular field monitoring for early detection

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Common rust is a widespread fungal disease that affects corn, causing reddish-brown pustules on the leaves.

Yellowing and wilting of the plant
treatment: Use of fungicides such as Propiconazole or Azoxystrobin
Plant resistant varieties or apply organic fungicides
prevention: Practice crop rotation to break the disease cycle
Remove and destroy infected plants to prevent spread

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Northern Leaf Blight is a fungal disease that causes long, grayish lesions on the corn leaves, significantly reducing yield.
symptoms: Long, elliptical, grey-green lesions on leaves
Lesions turn tan or gray as the disease progresses
treatment: Application of fungicides such as Propiconazole or Pyraclostrobin
Use of organic biocontrol agents like Trichoderma
prevention: Timely removal and destruction of infected plant debris
Maintain optimal plant density to promote air circulation

Grape___Black_rot.description: Black rot is a fungal disease affecting grapes, caused by Guignardia bidwellii.
symptoms: Dark, reddish-brown spots on leaves and fruit
Blighted young shoots, tendrils, and leaf petioles
treatment: Use of fungicides like Mancozeb and Ziram
Pruning and destroying infected parts
prevention: Proper pruning to promote air circulation

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: Esca, also known as Black Measles, is a serious fungal disease of grapevines that can cause leaf discoloration, fruit rot, and vine death.
symptoms: Decay or black spots on the fruit
treatment: Remove and destroy affected vines
Apply systemic fungicides
prevention: Regularly prune and monitor vines for early detection of symptoms
Maintain proper spacing between vines for adequate air circulation

treatment: Use of fungicides like mancozeb or chlorothalonil
Pruning and destruction of infected plant parts
prevention: Maintain good air circulation to prevent damp conditions

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: Huanglongbing, also known as citrus greening, is a serious bacterial disease that affects the vascular system of citrus trees, leading to premature fruit drop and death of the tree.
symptoms: Yellowing and blotchy mottle appearing on the leaves
Fruits are small and have a bitter taste
Branch dieback and eventually the entire tree wilts
treatment: Application of systemic insecticides like imidacloprid to control the vector, Asian citrus psyllid
Antibiotic treatment using products like streptomycin or oxytetracycline
prevention: Regular inspection and removal of infected trees to limit disease spread
Use of disease-free nursery plants for new plantings

Prune and destroy infected branches
prevention: Regularly inspect trees for early signs of disease

Fruit rot with fluffy white fungal growth under humid conditions
treatment: Use specific fungicides like Metalaxyl or Dimethomorph
Apply organic treatments like copper-based sprays or biofungicides

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Tomato leaf mold is a fungus disease caused by Passalora fulva that primarily affects the leaves of the tomato plant.
symptoms: Pale green spots on the upper leaf surface
Velvety, purple to brown mold on the lower leaf surface
treatment: Use fungicides containing chlorothalonil or mancozeb
Apply organic treatments such as copper fungicides or baking soda sprays
prevention: Ensure proper plant spacing for good air circulation
Water plants at the base to avoid wetting the leaves

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Septoria leaf spot is a common fungal disease in tomatoes that causes brown or grey spots on leaves.
symptoms: Brown/grey spots on leaves with a white or grey center
treatment: Use a specific fungicide like Chlorothalonil or Copper-based fungicides
Organic treatments include sprays with bicarbonate or copper soap
prevention: Ensure sufficient space between plants for good air circulation
Avoid water splashing as it spreads the disease, water the base of the plant instead

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Two-spotted spider mite is a common pest that affects tomato plants, causing damage by sucking sap from the underside of leaves.
symptoms: Visible tiny mites, eggs, or webs on the underside of leaves
Yellow or white speckles on leaves
treatment: Use a miticide specifically designed for spider mites
Introduce natural predators like ladybugs or lacewings
prevention: Regularly check the underside of leaves for signs of infestation
Maintain lower temperatures and higher humidity as mites prefer hot, dry conditions

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Tomato Target Spot is a fungal disease causing spots on leaves, stems and fruits of tomatoes.
treatment: Apply fungicides like chlorothalonil or mancozeb
Use organic fungicides like copper-based sprays
prevention: Practice crop rotation to reduce disease build-up
Avoid overhead irrigation to keep foliage dry

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Tomato mosaic virus is a disease that causes mottled yellowing of the leaves, stunted growth, and reduced yield in tomato plants.
treatment: Use of specific antiviral chemicals like Virucides
Removal and destruction of infected plants to prevent spread
prevention: Regular disinfection of tools and equipment

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus is a disease that causes yellowing and curling of tomato leaves, leading to stunted growth and reduced yield.
symptoms: Yellowing and upward curling of leaves
treatment: Application of Imidacloprid or Acetamiprid insecticides
Use of neem oil or insecticidal soap
prevention: Control whitefly population as they spread the virus
Regularly monitor plants for early detection of the disease
Remove and destroy infected plants immediately
